Rescheduling of the capital planning presentation was left to the chair and town manager.

what_happened.line: The town manager presented a proposed FY2015 budget covering revenue, state aid, insurance, retirement, departments, capital and the school gap.
The proposed budget leaves the schools short of the superintendent's request, partly offset by net metering credits.
The committee set the general reserve guideline at not more than half of one percent of the omnibus budget.
The committee worded the regular borrowing limit as a percentage of budgeted expenditures or of net levy, whichever is lower.
The policy author was given two weeks to return revised fiscal policies; the chair and town manager will reschedule the capital planning presentation.

why_it_matters: The reserve and borrowing limits set how much the town can borrow and hold back, which bears on future debt costs and the tax levy.
The school funding gap and the sharp rise in the retirement assessment bear on what the town budget, mostly taxes, can cover, and on what Town Meeting will be asked to vote.
watch_next: Revised fiscal policies are due back from the policy author within two weeks of this meeting.
A new date for the capital planning presentation, to be set by the chair and town manager.
